title: Safe methods: a safety plan, crisp chips and clean drying

say: Safe methods: a safety plan, crisp chips, and clean drying.
This is the video for Module 2 of Small-Scale Food Processing.
The World Health Organization gives five keys to safer food. First, keep clean. Wash hands and tools, and keep insects, rats and pets out.

panel.heading: The WHO Five Keys to Safer Food
items: Use safe water and raw materials

say: Second, separate raw and cooked. Use separate bowls, trays and boards.

panel.heading: The WHO Five Keys to Safer Food
items: Use safe water and raw materials

say: Third, cook thoroughly. Roast and fry until fully done inside, not just browned outside.

panel.heading: The WHO Five Keys to Safer Food
items: Use safe water and raw materials

say: Fourth, keep food at safe temperatures. Between 5 C and 60 C, bacteria multiply fast. Do not leave moist cooked food out for more than 2 hours.

panel.heading: The WHO Five Keys to Safer Food
items: Use safe water and raw materials

say: Fifth, use safe water, and reject mouldy or damaged raw food.

panel.heading: The WHO Five Keys to Safer Food
items: Use safe water and raw materials

say: HACCP means Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points. A hazard is anything that can make food unsafe: biological, like mould; chemical, like aflatoxin or cyanide; or physical, like stones or hair.

say: Next, pick the critical control points. These are the steps where control is essential.

say: At each one, set a critical limit you can check with your eyes, hands or a thermometer. For chips, oil at 160 C to 180 C.

say: And write it down every batch, on one page you stick on the wall.

panel.rule: A limit you cannot measure is not a limit.

say: For example, Halima in Kaduna makes groundnut paste. Her main danger is aflatoxin, a poison made by moulds. Roasting does not destroy it reliably, and long-term exposure is linked to liver cancer.
So her critical control point is sorting. Her limit: no mouldy, shrivelled or discoloured nuts, and no stones. If mould is widespread, the whole lot is rejected.

cards.d: No mouldy, shrivelled or discoloured nuts and no stones. Checks every tray by eye.
Cracks a few nuts open: evenly roasted, dry and crunchy throughout.
Checks the shared mill is clean, runs a small handful through first and discards it.

say: At roasting, she cracks a few nuts open to check they are dry and crunchy throughout.

say: Now a full chips batch. Use firm, fully green plantain. Wash before peeling, and oil your hands or wear gloves against the sap.

panel.heading: A plantain chips batch
items: Firm green plantain, washed and peeled
Heat oil to 160 C to 180 C
Seal, label with date and batch

say: Slice evenly, about 1 to 2 mm. A hand slicer works far better than a knife. Thin slices burn while thick ones stay soft.

say: Heat the oil to 160 C to 180 C, checked with a thermometer. Too cool and chips soak up oil. Too hot and they burn outside.

say: Fry in small batches. Overloading the pot drops the oil temperature.

say: Drain on a rack and cool completely under a clean net. Warm chips in a pouch release steam and go soft.

panel.rule: Cool chips completely before sealing, or they go soft.

say: Seal with an impulse sealer and label with the date and batch number.
Keep water away from hot oil, and change oil when it turns dark, smells sharp or smokes.

say: Write down weights at each stage, so you plan from real numbers. For example, Chiamaka in Onitsha weighs 10 fingers at 3.0 kg.
After peeling there is about 1.9 kg of flesh.
After frying, about 0.85 kg of chips remain, because most of the water is gone.
That fills 21 pouches of 40 g. Now she can plan purchases and costing from real numbers instead of guesses.
Drying on bare ground lets in dust, stones, droppings and insects, and slow drying in humid weather invites mould.
Use a raised rack covered with net, or a solar dryer. Spread food in one thin layer, turn it daily, and cover it at night and before rain.
Cool first, then test. Pieces should snap. Then seal a handful in a dry jar for a day. Droplets mean more drying.
For example, Grace's 5 kg of fresh pepper dried down to about 0.6 kg. Pack once it is cool, store it off the floor, and never add insecticides to stored food.

panel.heading: Test, pack and store
items: Store off the floor, first in first out

say: To remember. Follow the five keys. Give every critical point a limit, a check, a fix and a record. Control aflatoxin by sorting and dry storage. Fry at the right temperature and cool before sealing. And dry food off the ground, then test it.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Keep clean, separate, cook, safe temperatures, safe water
A CCP needs a limit, a check, a fix and a record
Aflatoxin: sort well and store dry
Fry at 160 C to 180 C and cool before sealing
Dry off the ground; snap test and jar test

say: Now write your one-page safety plan, fry a small test batch and record its weights, and dry one product, then check it weekly for four weeks.
